Thanks again for taking the time today  great conversation. Quick recap + proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary
- Goal: Integrate Redwood for account-level chat + customer-facing retrieval + reranking (embeddings + reranker) into FinTechApps support flow.
- Primary priorities you called out: simple SDK onboarding (TS + Python samples), local testing before cloud deployment, clear auth and data control options, and a path to structured output / tool calling for CRM updates.

Action items (owner / ETA)
1) Share SDK quickstart bundle (Python + TS samples, Docker compose for local testing)  Marissa / today (attached).
2) Architecture diagram + recommended routing/auth patterns for mixed workload (chat vs. async embeddings)  Dev / 6/9 EOD (attached).
3) Answer questions on embeddings storage, encryption, and local CPU testing  Dev / 6/9 morning.
4) Schedule 30-min integration call to walk the SEs through the sample app and auth flow  Laura to propose times for 6/106/11.

Notes on the quickstart we attached:
- Includes a minimal TypeScript sample and a Python Flask sample that demonstrate: API key auth, OIDC option for private deployments, local testing with docker-compose that spins up a small redis prefix cache and a lightweight mock for your internal user store.
- Routing: sample shows request headers with region/model preference and how to set fallbacks to smaller quantized variants for cost-sensitive paths.
- Structured output: the TS sample includes an example tool-calling handler (CRM update stub) using Redwoods structured schema output so you can validate and map fields before committing changes.
- Embeddings: sample shows sending embeddings to your customer-managed S3 (we include uploader helper). Reranker example included (simple cross-encoder scoring) to illustrate precision gains.

Next steps from you
- Confirm which environment you want to test first (local CPU vs dev GCP project).
- Any constraints around customer-managed keys / KMS we should know about.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.zip, arch-diagram.png, SOC2-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks  happy to hop on a call to walk through the samples.

Great questions  answers below. Short version: yes, you can keep embeddings in your S3 with CMEK; local testing on CPU is supported for the SDK flow (model quality/latency differs); and OIDC/service-account perms are minimal. Details: 

1) Embeddings & storage
- You can store embeddings in your S3 bucket (we provide an uploader helper in the quickstart that writes vectors + metadata to your bucket). For production we recommend using CMEK; Redwood accepts links to customer-managed S3 and will not ingest raw data unless explicitly configured.
- Reranker: for best accuracy we run the cross-encoder on GPU in the Dedicated path, but the quickstart includes a CPU fallback binary so you can exercise the logic locally. The quickstart also shows how to toggle a cheaper bi-encoder + FAISS index for fast candidates.

2) Local testing (Mac M1/M2)
- The TS sample uses the Redwood CLI local-mode and a lightweight mock model that runs in CPU mode. You can run end-to-end: generate -> embedding -> local rerank fallback. Performance will be slower, but the flow is identical. We include a docker-compose.yml with an x86_64 CPU container image (Rosetta if needed) and a README section for Apple silicon notes.
- If you want to test higher-fidelity reranking, we can provide a small cloud dev instance (gpu-rt-small) and temporary credits to run a couple of test episodes.

3) Auth & perms (OIDC/service account)
- Minimum permissions we need for the integration test path: basic token exchange (sts:TokenExchange) + read/write to the customer bucket if you want Redwood to push artifacts (optional). For private deployments we support OIDC tokens mapped to internal roles; AWS IAM role assumption or GCP service accounts are both supported.

Resources included in the quickstart:
- quickstart/ts-app/ (TypeScript sample with tool-calling handler)
- quickstart/python-flask/
- docker-compose.yml for local-mode
- scripts/upload_embeddings.sh (S3 helper)
- examples/reranker_cpu_fallback.py

Let me know if you want the sample modified to point to a temporary dev bucket  I can patch and re-share before the call.


